citeAs: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He (2023). C-Eval: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models. 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023) Track on Datasets and Benchmarks.
creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua University, University of Edinburgh, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)
description: C-Eval is the first comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context. It comprises 13,948 multiple-choice questions across 52 diverse disciplines (ranging from humanities to science and engineering) at four difficulty levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional. It is accompanied by C-Eval HARD, a subset of particularly challenging subjects requiring advanced reasoning abilities.
name: C-Eval
publisher: HKUST NLP Group (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)
rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators are the paper authors, who are researchers affiliated with Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua University, University of Edinburgh, and The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Manual annotation by the paper authors; GPT-4 API used for initial explanation generation
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions underwent several rounds of human validation by the authors. For the development split, five exemplars per subject were annotated with step-by-step explanations to enable few-shot chain-of-thought evaluation. Explanations were first generated automatically by prompting GPT-4, then manually revised by the authors (Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, and Junxian He) to obtain final high-quality explanations.
rai:dataBiases: The paper acknowledges that English benchmarks tend to exhibit geographical biases towards the domestic knowledge of the regions that produce them, which motivated the creation of C-Eval for Chinese contexts. To mitigate data contamination bias, questions were collected from mock exams or small-scale local exams rather than exact questions from official national exams (which are widely distributed online and may have been crawled into LLM pretraining data). The distribution of correct answers shows slight fluctuations around the random 25% level (A: 22.9%, B: 26.0%, C: 26.4%, D: 24.7%), similar to MMLU, indicating minor option bias.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from mock exams and small-scale local exams freely available on the internet (primarily as PDF or Microsoft Word documents, and a minor fraction as web pages), as well as past exam questions from top universities in China publicly shared by students. A minor fraction of college questions are mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam sourced from the Weipu website, for which authorization was obtained to include around 2000 such questions. Questions were collected across four difficulty levels (middle school, high school, college, professional) spanning 52 disciplines. The authors deliberately avoided using exact questions from official national exams to mitigate data contamination.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists primarily of mock exam questions in PDF or Microsoft Word document formats, with a minor fraction as web pages. A portion of college-level questions are past exam questions from top Chinese universities shared by students. Around 2000 questions are mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam from the Weipu website.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: C-Eval, along with all English-language benchmarks, is far from perfect for LLM evaluation. It does not cover many other abilities such as reasoning over and calling APIs, and does not assess multiple aspects beyond accuracy, including safety, bias, and robustness. The benchmark is limited to multiple-choice format questions. The test split labels are kept private to ensure fair use, requiring users to submit predictions to the website for evaluation.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF documents were initially processed into text. All questions were subsequently parsed — automatically when possible, and otherwise manually by the authors — into a structured format. For subjects with complex mathematical notations (e.g., STEM subjects), LaTeX formats were manually applied. All questions were processed to include exactly four choices: questions with fewer than four options were eliminated, and incorrect choices were randomly dropped for questions with more than four options. Questions went through standard data preprocessing including deduplication and cleaning. LaTeX notations were ensured to compile without syntax errors. Questions were randomly split into development, validation, and test sets within each subject at a 1:9 ratio for validation and test.
rai:dataSocialImpact: C-Eval is intended to help analyze important strengths and shortcomings of foundation models and foster their development and growth for Chinese users. It aims to narrow the gap between Chinese LLM development and evaluation, providing a standard for assessing LLMs in a Chinese context beyond simple conversational tasks. The benchmark is designed to guide developers in preparing LLMs to function in more complex scenarios relevant to Chinese society.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of large language models (LLMs) and foundation models in a Chinese context. Assessing LLMs across multiple dimensions including STEM, humanities, social science, and other areas at four difficulty levels. Analyzing important strengths and shortcomings of foundation models to guide developers in improving their models for Chinese users. Benchmarking Chinese-oriented and English-oriented LLMs on Chinese knowledge and reasoning tasks.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to automatically generate step-by-step explanations for the development split exemplars, which were subsequently manually revised by the authors.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The paper does not specify a fixed number of independent annotations per item; validation was done through cross-validation rounds by the authors collectively.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No inter-annotator agreement metrics or formal annotation quality analysis are reported in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not discuss missing data handling in the collection process.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe or date range for data collection is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation of missing values is described; not applicable to this exam question dataset.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection augmentation, balancing, or resampling of the dataset itself is described beyond standard preprocessing.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists of exam questions and does not contain personal or sensitive information about individuals.
